summaries.summary: Learner corpora have been compiled for English and increasingly for other languages, including French, Spanish, and Italian resources.

Portuguese learner corpora include Leiria corpus with 470 texts and 70,500 tokens, COPLE2 with 1,058 texts and 201,921 tokens, PEAPL2 with 516 texts and 119,381 tokens, and CAL2 with 1,380 texts and 281,301 words.
Portuguese learner corpora support Native Language Identification (NLI), which determines an author’s L1 from L2 productions and motivates second language acquisition research.
Existing Portuguese data for NLI face limitations involving varying L1 backgrounds, limited POS-tag annotation in PEAPL2 and COPLE2, and different data formats.
The paper presents NLI-PT, a freely available Portuguese NLI dataset unifying learner data in a unified format with uniform linguistic annotation.
NLI has attracted attention, especially for English, with notable NLI shared task editions organized in 2013 and 2017.
Recent NLI studies include Arabic and Chinese, while no Portuguese study has been published and NLI-PT enables Portuguese research with first simple baseline results.
NLI-PT can support other applications, and Portuguese educational NLP studies include grammatical error correction, automated essay scoring, academic word lists, and learner corpora.
Data was collected from three Portuguese learner corpora: COPLE2, Leiria corpus, and PEAPL2.

The three corpora contain written productions from Portuguese learners with different proficiency levels and native languages (L1s), with all COPLE2 data and sections of PEAPL2 and Leiria corpus included.

Text selection used specific L1s, with COPLE2 as reference and 15 L1s included: Chinese, English, Spanish, German, Russian, French, Japanese, Italian, Dutch, Tetum, Arabic, Polish, Korean, Romanian, and Swedish.
Leiria corpus and PEAPL2 use 36 stimuli or topics, while COPLE2 has 149 different topics reorganized to 112 in the dataset.
The 148 topics are not uniformly represented: three topics account for 48.7% of texts, 72% have 1-10 texts, and text lengths range from 16 to 787 tokens.
The three corpora use CEFR proficiency levels, with A1, A2, B1, B2, and C1 in COPLE2 and PEAPL2, and A, B, and C in Leiria corpus.
The learner corpora use different formats, so transcription annotations were removed from PEAPL2 and Leiria files before linguistic annotation with NLP tools.
The dataset was annotated at Part of Speech (POS) and syntax levels using LX Parser, Freeling, and DepPattern toolkit for simple POS, detailed POS, constituency, and dependency annotations.
NLI-PT was developed primarily for NLI but can be used for second language acquisition and educational NLP applications.
The first lexical baseline for Portuguese NLI uses a sub-set of NLI-PT and fills the gap in published Portuguese NLI studies.
A simple linear SVM classifier with a bag of words model used five L1s: Chinese (355 texts), English (236 texts), German (214 texts), Italian (216 texts), and Spanish (271 texts).
Stratified 10-fold cross-validation achieved 70% accuracy, but the experiment does not account for topic bias because NLI-PT is not balanced by topic.
NLI-PT is the first Portuguese dataset compiled for NLI, containing 1,868 texts by speakers of 15 L1s and over 380,000 tokens.
NLI-PT supports research beyond NLI, and a bag of words model with Chinese, English, German, Italian, and Spanish texts achieved 70% accuracy.
Future work will include more texts in the dataset following the same methodology and annotation.
The authors thank Centro de Estudos de Linguística Geral e Aplicada at Universidade de Coimbra and Centro de Linguística da Universidade de Lisboa for making data available.
This work was partially supported by Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia under postdoctoral research grant SFRH/BPD/109914/2015.
